records.title: Lung cancer (NSCLC & SCLC)
records.subtitle: Thoracic · IASLC/UICC 9th ed. (TNM) · IASLC 9th, 2024 (effective Jan 2025)
records.body: TNM True Same TNM applies to NSCLC and SCLC (SCLC is additionally described as limited- vs extensive-stage for treatment). 9th edition (IASLC/UICC), in effect from 1 January 2025; AJCC's published manual remains 8th edition. Changes from the 8th edition: T descriptors unchanged; N2 split into N2a (single ipsilateral mediastinal/subcarinal station) and N2b (multiple stations); M1c split into M1c1 (multiple metastases in one organ system) and M1c2 (multiple metastases in more than one organ system). Key stage-group shifts: T1N1 IIB→IIA; T1N2a IIIA→IIB; T3N2a IIIB→IIIA; T2a/bN2b IIIA→IIIB. Superior sulcus (Pancoast) tumours: arise at the lung apex with invariable chest wall / parietal-pleural invasion, making them T3 at minimum regardless of size. T3 if invasion is limited to chest wall / parietal pleura / first rib, thoracic nerve roots T1 or T2 (lower brachial plexus), and/or the stellate ganglion. T4 if any of: C8 nerve root or above (cervical roots, including brachial plexus cords or trunks); subclavian vessels; vertebral body, lamina, or spinal canal. Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis) marks stellate-ganglion involvement (T3), but C8-root involvement also produces Horner and is T4 — MRI is the arbiter when cord/trunk extension is suspected. Stage-group consequences: T3N0 = IIB; T3–T4N1 or T4N0 = IIIA; T3N2a = IIIA (9th-ed change from IIIB); T3N2b or T4N2 = IIIB; T3–T4N3 = IIIC. Standard resectable approach (T3–T4N0–N1): induction concurrent chemoradiation → surgery. Source: RadioGraphics 2024 (DOI 10.1148/rg.240057); T descriptors unchanged from IASLC 8th ed. records.title: Diffuse pleural mesothelioma
records.subtitle: Thoracic · IASLC/UICC 9th ed. (TNM) · IASLC 9th, 2024 (effective Jan 2025)
records.body: TNM True Applies to diffuse pleural mesothelioma only (not localised pleural tumours or peritoneal mesothelioma). 9th edition (IASLC/UICC/AJCC), in effect from 1 January 2025. Major change — the clinical T (cT) is now measurement-based: summed maximal pleural thickness on CT at three hemithorax levels (Psum; cutpoints 12 and 30 mm) plus fissural involvement (Fmax >5 mm), replacing the 8th-edition qualitative invasion descriptors that proved unreliable on CT (endothoracic fascia, lung-parenchymal invasion and non-transmural diaphragm invasion were removed). cT4 (unresectable invasion) is unchanged. Pathological T (pT) retains the 8th-edition anatomical descriptors, with the one change that fissural involvement is now pT2 (was pT1): pT1 = ipsilateral parietal ± visceral/mediastinal/diaphragmatic pleura without fissural involvement; pT2 = diaphragmatic-muscle invasion, lung-parenchymal extension, or fissural involvement; pT3 = locally advanced, potentially resectable; pT4 = locally advanced, unresectable. N and M categories are unchanged from the 8th edition. Stage groups were revised and clinical and pathological groupings now align — the 8th-edition IA/IB split is gone (T1N0 = stage I); any T3 = IIIA; any T4 = IIIB. The T column below shows the clinical cT; stage groups apply to both clinical and pathological staging. cT1 Psum (summed maximal pleural thickness on CT, three levels) ≤12 mm, without fissural involvement cT2 Psum >12–30 mm; or any tumour with fissural involvement (Fmax >5 mm) cT3 Psum >30 mm cT4 Locally advanced, technically unresectable — invasion of diffuse/multifocal chest wall, peritoneum (transdiaphragmatic), contralateral pleura, mediastinal organs, spine, or transmural pericardium/myocardium (unchanged from 8th ed.) records.title: Thymoma & thymic carcinoma
records.subtitle: Thoracic · Masaoka–Koga (modified, 1994) · Masaoka–Koga 1994 (ITMIG-defined)
records.body: other True Masaoka–Koga (Koga 1994 modification of the 1981 Masaoka system), the long-standing surgical-pathological staging for thymic epithelial tumours, as clarified by ITMIG (Detterbeck et al., 2011). Stage reflects the extent of invasion found at resection and remains widely used and prognostic. The AJCC/UICC 8th-edition TNM (IASLC/ITMIG) is the formal current system; Masaoka–Koga is shown here by preference. Completeness of resection (R0/R1/R2) is independently prognostic. Masaoka–Koga stage I Macroscopically and microscopically completely encapsulated (no capsular invasion) IIa Microscopic transcapsular invasion IIb Macroscopic invasion into thymic or surrounding fatty tissue, or grossly adherent to but not through the mediastinal pleura or pericardium III Macroscopic invasion into neighbouring organs (pericardium, great vessels, or lung) IVa Pleural or pericardial dissemination IVb Lymphogenous or haematogenous metastasis Masaoka–Koga

records.body: TNM True Anal canal squamous cell carcinoma. AJCC Version 9, effective 1 January 2023 (CAP required use: March 2023). T and N category definitions are largely unchanged from the 8th edition (T by size, not depth; N by nodal group), except obturator nodes are now included in N1a. The stage groups were reordered because 8th-edition data showed a hierarchy violation — stage IIIA (T1-2 N1) had better survival than IIB (T3 N0), i.e. T category outweighs N for anal cancer. Changes from 8th ed.: stage 0 (Tis / HSIL) removed from the staging system (a precursor lesion, not invasive cancer); IIB redefined T3N0 → T1-2 N1; IIIA redefined T1-2 N1 → T3 N0-1; IIIC redefined T3-4 N1 → T4 N1. Net effect: T3N0 moves up (IIB→IIIA) while T1-2 N1 moves down (IIIA→IIB). records.body: TNM True AJCC/UICC 9th version (TNM-9), launched for global use January 2025. Changes from the 8th edition: (1) T category unchanged in substance (wording clarified). (3) Stage restructured — all M0 disease is now stage I-III. Stage I expanded to T1-2 N0-1 and split into IA (T1-2 N0) and IB (T1-2 N1) for treatment guidance; the old 8th-ed stage III (T3 / N2) becomes stage II, and old IVA (T4 / N3) becomes stage III. Still purely anatomic; plasma EBV-DNA is prognostic but not yet incorporated. T0 = occult primary with EBV-positive cervical node, grouped as T1. T and M are unchanged; Tis / stage 0 do not exist in p16+ disease (tonsillar crypt epithelium lacks a basement membrane). Clinical stage-group criteria are unchanged, so cases migrate via cN rather than new groupings (ICON-N: Huang et al. 2025). PATHOLOGICAL (pTNM9): pENE becomes a pN modifier and node count is formalised — pN1 (1-4 nodes, pENE−) splits into pN1a (1 node) / pN1b (2-4 nodes); pN2 = 1-4 nodes pENE+ or >4 nodes pENE−; pN3 = >4 nodes pENE+. Revised pathological stage groups: I = pT0-2 N0-N1; II = pT0-2 N2-N3 or pT3 N0-N2; III = pT3 N3 or any pT4; IV = M1 (Ho et al. 2025). iENE/pENE are assigned only on unequivocal/definitive evidence; their grade or extent is not staged. records.subtitle: Head & Neck · AJCC v9 / UICC 9th ed. (TNM) · AJCC Version 9, 2026 (UICC TNM9)
records.body: TNM True AJCC Version 9 / UICC TNM 9th edition, effective 1 January 2026 — the first unified staging system for both major and minor salivary gland carcinoma (the 8th edition covered major glands only; minor SGCs were previously staged by site of origin). Changes from the 8th edition: (1) N is simplified and decoupled from the generic head & neck scheme, now count-based — N0 none, N1 1-3 nodes ENE-negative, N2 >3 nodes or any ENE; the old N2a/N2b/N2c and N3 categories are gone. Node count = all positive nodes in the head & neck region (parotid + cervical). (2) T criteria are unchanged in substance, but the wording was clarified: T3 = 'gross extraparenchymal extension' (a T3 criterion for MAJOR SGC only — clinical/macroscopic, not microscopic; minor SGCs are staged by size alone for T1-T3), and T4a anchored on 'bone invasion'. T category now also covers SGCs of the trachea, cervical oesophagus, middle ear and intraosseous (central) jaw. (3) Stage IV is reserved for M1 disease only; all M0 disease is stage I-III. (4) Clinical TNM (cTNM) uses the same criteria as pTNM, with imaging-detected ENE (iENE) and radiologic node count. (5) Excluded histologies: squamous cell, neuroendocrine and basosquamous carcinoma (usually non-salivary/cutaneous origin); carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma is no longer a distinct type. No carcinoma-in-situ (Tis) category in the v9 table. records.body: FIGO True FIGO 2023 staging shown (surgical + pathological). Major change: stage now depends on histological type. Non-aggressive = low-grade (G1–2) endometrioid; aggressive = high-grade (G3) endometrioid, serous, clear-cell, undifferentiated, mixed, mesonephric-like, gastrointestinal-mucinous, and carcinosarcoma. LVSI: focal 2 mm; micrometastasis 0.2–2 mm or >200 cells; isolated tumour cells (≤0.2 mm/≤200 cells) = pN0(i+), do NOT upstage. IA3 (synchronous low-grade endometrial + ovarian) requires all of: <50% myometrial invasion, no substantial LVSI, no other metastasis, unilateral ovary confined without capsule breach (else IIIA1). Molecular subtype adds an 'm' suffix — see the molecular modifiers below. IA1 Non-aggressive type limited to an endometrial polyp, or confined to the endometrium IA2 Non-aggressive type, <50% myometrial invasion, no or focal LVSI IA3 Low-grade endometrioid limited to uterus AND ovary (synchronous, meeting all criteria — see note) IB Non-aggressive type, ≥50% myometrial invasion, no or focal LVSI IC Aggressive type limited to a polyp or confined to the endometrium (no myometrial invasion) IIA Non-aggressive type invading cervical stroma IIB Non-aggressive type with substantial LVSI (≥5 vessels) IIC Aggressive type with any myometrial invasion IIIA1 Spread to ovary or fallopian tube (except when meeting IA3 criteria) IIIA2 Uterine subserosal involvement or spread through the uterine serosa IIIB1 Metastasis or direct spread to vagina and/or parametria IIIB2 Metastasis to the pelvic peritoneum IIIC1 Pelvic lymph node metastasis — IIIC1i micrometastasis / IIIC1ii macrometastasis IIIC2 Para-aortic lymph node metastasis up to renal vessels (± pelvic) — IIIC2i micro / IIIC2ii macro IVA Invasion of bladder and/or intestinal/bowel mucosa IVB Abdominal peritoneal metastasis beyond the pelvis IVC Distant metastasis (extra-/intra-abdominal nodes above renal vessels, lung, liver, brain, bone) Molecular modifiers ('m' suffix; Stage I–II only) IAmPOLEmut POLEmut carcinoma confined to corpus or with cervical extension — regardless of LVSI or histology (downstaged) IICmp53abn p53abn carcinoma confined to corpus with any myometrial invasion, ± cervical invasion — regardless of LVSI or histology (upstaged) MMRd / NSMP Do not change the stage; record as Stage Im (data collection only). In Stage III–IV molecular subtype never alters stage (recorded as IIIm/IVm). FIGO

records.body: other True Grade (Ki-67 / mitotic rate) is the dominant prognostic axis; well-differentiated NET (G1–G3) is distinguished from poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC). records.title: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour (panNET)
records.subtitle: Gastrointestinal · AJCC v9 (TNM = 8th ed.) · AJCC Version 9, 2023 (req. Jan 2024)
records.body: TNM True Applies to well-differentiated pancreatic NET. AJCC Version 9 (GEP-NET protocol, required from 1 Jan 2024) keeps the 8th-edition T/N/M and stage groups unchanged for the pancreas — and, unlike gastric/duodenal/colorectal/appendiceal NETs, the pancreas did NOT adopt the v9 T1NXM0→stage I change.
